🧠 Crypto News Brief: Crypto spent the weekend digesting the largest theft in its history: the FBI named North Korea, Binance reopened withdrawals and Bitcoin steadied near $78K. Fresh breaches and Beijing's crackdown kept sentiment cautious. 🕵️ FBI Blames North Korea for $6B Binance Heist The FBI said on Saturday that North Korea's TraderTraitor hacking unit was behind the theft of more than $6 billion from Binance, the largest crypto heist on record. Working with the Secret Service and IRS-CI, the bureau says the attackers are swapping the loot mainly into ether and are expected to launder it through DeFi and instant-swap services. Read full story 🔓 Binance Reopens Withdrawals, Covers 95% of Losses Binance began restoring withdrawals on Sunday, starting with bitcoin and adding ether, USDT, USDC, BNB and XRP across 15 other blockchains, with remaining assets returning only after security checks. The exchange now says it has covered about 95% of the stolen amount, up from 90%, and insists users will not absorb the loss. More details 📈 Bitcoin Steadies Near $78K After Hack Sell-Off Bitcoin climbed back toward $78,000 on Sunday, recovering from the Binance-driven sell-off that dragged it to a six-week low near $76,100. Major coins traded in a narrow weekend range, while Lighter (LIT) led the altcoin pack with a gain of roughly 18%. Read more 🇨🇳 China's Communist Party Targets Crypto Bribery A Central Committee resolution published by Xinhua on November 1 calls for a tougher fight against corruption carried out through virtual currencies, blockchain and cross-border capital flows. Investigators are told to pursue officials who use digital assets to take bribes or hide illicit wealth, while China's existing crypto trading restrictions stay in force. See details 🤖 AI-Assisted Hacker Breaches Chainalysis Blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis disclosed that an attacker using AI-driven agentic techniques broke into its systems and internal tools this month, accessing customer names, emails, user IDs and role labels. The company says credentials, session tokens and investigation data were not touched, and that the incident is unrelated to the Binance theft. Does it really matter which rice you eat?



Sam Wikeley

Science correspondent



 Occasionally, when standing in the supermarket aisle, my hand will hover over a bag of brown rice. Conventional wisdom suggests it is healthier than its white counterpart and, indeed, it does contain more fibre, magnesium and other wholesome nutrients. Personal experience, however, suggests it is far less delicious. Shamefully, that latter consideration usually outweighs the former, and I grab a bag of white rice instead.
